newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-LOPEZ KEEPS TITLE AGAINST A COURAGEOUS THAI.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-LOPEZ KEEPS TITLE AGAINST A COURAGEOUS THAI.

text.p: World Boxing Council (WBC) strawwweight champion Ricardo Lopez of Mexico surprisingly was forced to go the distance by unheralded Thai challenger Mongol Charoen to win his 19th consecutive title defence on Saturday.
Lopez, 45-0, who was bleeding over his right eye after an accidental head butt in the 10th round, had to fight until the final bell for only the fourth time in his professional career.
Lopez was given every round by judges Carol Castellano and Martin Sammon, 120-107 and judge Joraicio Castillo scored it 119-108.
Chareon, 18, the 10th rated challenger by the WBC and was fighting for the first time out of his homeland and had only arrived here five days before the bout.
"He was well prepared," Lopez said of Charoen, 17-2. "He surprsied me how tough he was. I was surprised he didn't go down."
Chareon had a bloody nose after the first round and continued to absorb a lot more punishment from the champion's stinging head and body apunches.

Charoen took a pounding throughout the fight but particularly in the 11th round, starting with a right to the nose. But Charoen, showing tremendous courage and a concrete chin, managed to stand up to the assault. The challenger refused to go down late in the 12th round after Lopez's unloaded four rights to the head.
"I am very proud to have gone the distance with Lopez," said Charoen.
Chareon was deducted a point by referee Jay Nady for the head butt that left Lopez with blood streaming down the side of his face.
"The blood didn't scare me, but it did worry me ," Lopez said of the cut. "I had to be careful."
Lopez has held the title since 1990 the longest of any reigning champion in boxing.
